record.paper_title: Open Questions in Massive Star Research across Cosmic Scales
record.context_brief: sgB[e] stars as hidden post-common-envelope systems
record.original_question: Are supergiant B[e] stars a missing evolutionary link in the formation of mid-type WN Wolf-Rayet binaries, by masking post-common-envelope systems behind circumstellar material? This question includes testing whether objects such as HD 38489 in the Large Magellanic Cloud and Wd1-9 in Westerlund 1 hide Wolf-Rayet plus OB-star binary configurations beneath B[e]-type spectra or circumstellar emission.

evidence.quote: A missing link in the formation of mid-type WN binaries could be sgB[e] stars, masking post-common envelope systems. In the LMC, the sgB[e] HD 38489 (aka LHA 120-S134) shows broad He II 4686 Å-emission within a B[e]-type spectrum (e.g, Massey et al. 2014) and many authors conclude that the B[e] phenomenon does not reflect the underlying object(s), but only shows the circumstellar material (e.g., Zickgraf et al. 1986; Clark et al. 2013).
Intestingly, the X-ray spectrum of the sgB[e] Wd1-9 also indicates a WR+OB binary (Anastasopoulou et al. 2025).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Supergiant B[e] stars (sgB[e]) are luminous, evolved early-type stars whose optical spectra are dominated by Balmer emission, low-excitation permitted and forbidden metallic emission lines, and a strong infrared excess attributed to hot circumstellar dust in a non-spherical (typically disk-like) envelope. It is widely held that the B[e] phenomenon reflects properties of the surrounding circumstellar material rather than of the underlying stellar object(s), so that a sgB[e] spectrum can in principle conceal the true nature of the central source(s), including the possibility that the central object is a binary system. A Wolf-Rayet (WR) star is a hot, hydrogen-depleted, high-mass-loss-rate evolved massive star; mid-type WN Wolf-Rayet stars are nitrogen-sequence WR stars of intermediate spectral subtype, and many are known to occur in close binaries with OB-type companions, where they are believed to descend from massive binaries that have undergone a common-envelope (CE) phase or other strong binary interaction.

Determine whether sgB[e] stars constitute a missing evolutionary link in the formation of mid-type WN + OB binary systems, in the sense that a non-trivial fraction of sgB[e] objects are post-common-envelope binaries whose WR + OB nature is hidden beneath optically thick circumstellar emission characteristic of the B[e] phenomenon. In particular, decide whether the sgB[e] stars HD 38489 (= LHA 120-S134) in the Large Magellanic Cloud and Wd1-9 in the young massive Galactic cluster Westerlund 1 host underlying WR + OB-star binaries concealed by their B[e]-type spectra and circumstellar emission.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature provides mounting but not yet conclusive evidence for the hypothesis. The X-ray spectrum of Wd1-9 has been interpreted as a WR+OB binary, and a related study of Wd1-72 frames it together with Wd1-9 as candidate post-interaction WN binaries, supporting the view that some sgB[e] stars hide post-common-envelope WR+OB systems. However, the general claim across the sgB[e] population, and the specific status of HD 38489, are not established, so the question remains only partially answered.

status_evidence.title: EWOCS-V: Is Wd1-72 a recent post-interaction WR+O binary?
status_evidence.snippet: If Wd1-72 and Wd1-9 represent different evolutionary stages of recent post-interaction WN binaries, then further study could help address how mass transfer shapes these systems.
status_evidence.claim: Wd1-9 is being analyzed as a candidate post-interaction WN+O binary, partially supporting the sgB[e]-as-hidden-post-CE-binary hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: A hidden population of Wolf-Rayet stars in Westerlund 1
status_evidence.snippet: Wd1-9 exhibits the rich optical emission line spectrum characteristic of sgB[e] stars within the coeval starburst cluster Westerlund 1.
status_evidence.claim: Wd1-9 is established as an sgB[e] star within a massive cluster context, consistent with concealment of an underlying evolved binary.
